1.title: RBAC, Service Accounts and Kubeconfig
1.text: Welcome to Module two: R back, Service Accounts and Kubeconfig. It covers the exam area Cluster Architecture, Installation and Configuration. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. How a request is checked. The four objects. Fast commands. Test it: kube control auth can i. A bug you will see: role Ref is immutable. Service accounts and tokens. Practice with six hands-on labs worth thirty-six points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Cluster Architecture, Installation and Configuration (twenty-five percent). Practice in this module: six labs, thirty-six points, about thirty-eight minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: How a request is checked
1.text: How a request is checked. Every A P I request passes three gates, in order: authentication (who are you?), authorization (may you do this?), admission (is the object acceptable?). R back is the authorization gate. It is additive: there are only allow rules, no deny rules. No matching rule means "forbidden".

1.title: How a request is checked, continued
1.text: How a request is checked. A user (human). A client certificate (the certificate's C N is the user name, O is the group) or an external identity. Kubernetes has no User object. A Service Account. A Kubernetes object; Pods use its token. Full name system serviceaccount namespace name. A group. A label on the identity, for example the certificate's O field.

1.title: The four objects
1.text: The four objects. The figure shows this: How R back objects connect. Exam tip: A Cluster Role used through a Role Binding gives access in one namespace only.

1.title: The four objects, continued
1.text: The four objects. Role. Scope: one namespace. Holds: permissions (rules). Cluster Role. Scope: whole cluster. Holds: permissions; also for cluster-scoped resources (nodes, namespaces, Persistent Volumes) and non-resource U R Ls. Role Binding. Scope: one namespace. Holds: who gets a Role or a Cluster Role inside that namespace. Cluster Role Binding. Scope: whole cluster. Holds: who gets a Cluster Role everywhere. The pattern the exam loves: a Cluster Role bound with a Role Binding grants those permissions only in that one namespace. The same Cluster Role bound with a Cluster Role Binding grants it everywhere. A rule has verbs ( get list watch create update patch delete ), resources ( pods, deployments ) and, for non-core resources, an A P I group ( apps for Deployments; the core group is ).

1.title: Fast commands (no YAML)
1.text: Fast commands (no yamel). The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Fast commands (no YAML), continued
1.text: Fast commands (no yamel). Resource with a group: the resource flag set to deployments dot apps. Service account subject format for the flag: namespace name ( the serviceaccount flag set to ci deployer ). A wrong namespace is a common bug. Built-in Cluster Roles you can reuse: view (read most things in a namespace), edit, admin, cluster admin.

1.title: Test it: kubectl auth can-i
1.text: Test it: kube control auth can i. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Verify every R back change with kube control auth can i and the the as flag flag before you move on.

1.title: Test it: kubectl auth can-i, continued
1.text: Test it: kube control auth can i. Always finish an R back task with can i: one "yes" and one "no" (a different namespace or verb) proves the scope.

1.title: A bug you will see: roleRef is immutable
1.text: A bug you will see: role Ref is immutable. A Role Binding's role Ref (which Role it points at) cannot be edited. If it names a Role that does not exist (a typo), kube control edit fails; delete and recreate the binding. Check with k dash n shop two get rolebinding app cm dash o yaml. The other common mistakes: the subject's namespace is wrong, or a Role Binding was used where a Cluster Role Binding is needed (or the reverse). Exam tip: The role Ref of a binding cannot be edited: delete the binding and create it again.

1.title: Service accounts and tokens
1.text: Service accounts and tokens. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Service accounts and tokens, continued
1.text: Service accounts and tokens. Every namespace has a default Service Account. Pods use it unless spec dot service Account Name says otherwise. Modern clusters do not auto-create long-lived token Secrets; use create token. Use the token as the token flag set to T O K E N against the A P I server to test what it can do.

1.title: Give a person a kubeconfig (CertificateSigningRequest flow)
1.text: Give a person a kube config (Certificate Signing Request flow). Make a private key and a C S R (Certificate Signing Request) whose subject is the user name: open S S L req -new -key jane dot key -subj slash C N jane -out jane dot csr. Submit a Certificate Signing Request with signer Name Kubernetes dot io slash kube A P I server client, usages client auth, and request set to the base sixty-four of the C S R (single line: base sixty-four -w zero ). Approve: k certificate approve jane. The signed certificate appears in dot status dot certificate (base sixty-four). Build the kube config. Exam tip: For a user certificate the signer is Kubernetes dot io slash kube A P I server client, the usage is client auth, and you must approve the request.

1.title: Give a person a kubeconfig (CertificateSigningRequest flow), continued
1.text: Give a person a kube config (Certificate Signing Request flow). The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Give a person a kubeconfig (CertificateSigningRequest flow), continued
1.text: Give a person a kube config (Certificate Signing Request flow). Proof: k the kube config flag jane dot kube config get pods works in dev and is forbidden elsewhere. A certificate alone gives no rights; the Role Binding does. Contexts in one line: a context equals cluster plus user plus namespace. kube control config get contexts, kube control config use context name, kube control config view the minify flag shows the active one.

1.title: Lab 2.1: role binding
1.text: Lab two point one: role binding. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace dev, create a Role pod reader that allows the verbs get, list and watch on Pods only. Bind it with a Role Binding named read pods to the user jane. The user must not be able to delete Pods, and must not be able to read Pods in other namespaces. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 2.1: role binding, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n dev create role pod reader the verb flag set to get,list,watch the resource flag set to pods. Then kube control dash n dev create rolebinding read pods the role flag set to pod reader the user flag set to jane. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 2.2: sa clusterrole
1.text: Lab two point two: sa clusterrole. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Create the namespace ci and a Service Account deployer in it. Create a Cluster Role deploy manager that allows get, list, create and update on deployments in the apps A P I group. Grant it to the Service Account only inside the namespace ci (not cluster-wide). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 2.2: sa clusterrole, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control create ns ci. Then kube control dash n ci create serviceaccount deployer. Then kube control create clusterrole deploy manager the verb flag set to get,list,create,update the resource flag set to deployments dot apps. Then kube control dash n ci create rolebinding deploy manager the clusterrole flag set to deploy manager the serviceaccount flag set to ci deployer. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 2.3: cluster wide read
1.text: Lab two point three: cluster wide read. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Members of the group auditors must be able to get and list Nodes and Namespaces across the whole cluster, and nothing else. Create a Cluster Role cluster auditor and a Cluster Role Binding auditors read for the group. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 2.3: cluster wide read, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control create clusterrole cluster auditor the verb flag set to get,list the resource flag set to nodes,namespaces. Then kube control create clusterrolebinding auditors read the clusterrole flag set to cluster auditor the group flag set to auditors. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 2.4: fix rolebinding
2.text: Lab two point four: fix rolebinding. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace shop two, the Service Account app cannot read Config Maps although a Role and a Role Binding exist. Find the mistake and fix it so that app can get and list Config Maps in shop two (and nothing outside that namespace). Keep the Role named cm reader and the Role Binding named app cm. Hint: some fields of a Role Binding cannot be edited; you may need to recreate it. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 2.4: fix rolebinding, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n shop two get rolebinding app cm dash o yaml then pipe to grep -A three role Ref. Then kube control dash n shop two delete rolebinding app cm. Then kube control dash n shop two create rolebinding app cm the role flag set to cm reader the serviceaccount flag set to shop two app. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 2.5: user certificate
2.text: Lab two point five: user certificate. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about ten minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. A new developer jane needs access. In the namespace dev, a Role and Role Binding already let the user jane list Pods. Create a private key and a certificate signing request for jane and submit a Certificate Signing Request object named jane (signer for A P I client certificates, usage client auth ). Approve it and fetch the issued certificate.

2.title: Lab 2.5: user certificate, continued
2.text: Lab two point five: user certificate, continued. Create a kube config file about slash answers slash jane dot kube config with a user jane (embedded credentials), the cluster of the current context, and a context jane ctx in the namespace dev that is the current context of that file. Prove it by running kube control the kube config flag about slash answers slash jane dot kube config get pods. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 2.5: user certificate, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run cd about slash answers. Then open S S L genrsa -out jane dot key two thousand forty-eight two slash dev slash null. Then open S S L req -new -key jane dot key -subj slash C N jane -out jane dot csr. kube control apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control certificate approve jane. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 2.5: user certificate, Solution, continued
2.text: Lab two point five: user certificate, Solution, continued. Run for i in seq one twenty do dash n kube control get csr jane dash o json path dot status dot certificate break sleep one done. Then kube control get csr jane dash o json path dot status dot certificate base sixty-four dash d jane dot crt. Then kube control config view the raw flag the minify flag dash o json path dot clusters zero dot cluster dot certificate authority data base sixty-four dash d ca dot crt. Then S E R V E R kube control config view the minify flag dash o json path dot clusters zero dot cluster dot server. Then kube control config set cluster kind C K A the server flag set to S E R V E R the certificate authority flag set to ca dot crt the embed certs flag set, and so on. Then kube control config set credentials jane the client certificate flag set to jane dot crt the client key flag set to jane dot key the embed certs flag set to true the kube config, and so on. Then kube control config set context jane ctx the cluster flag set to kind C K A the user flag set to jane the namespace flag set to dev the kube config flag set to, and so on. Then kube control config use context jane ctx the kube config flag set to jane dot kube config. Then kube control the kube config flag jane dot kube config get pods. The remaining lines are on the screen.

2.title: Lab 2.6: sa token
2.text: Lab two point six: sa token. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Create the namespace ops and a Service Account reporter in it. Give the Service Account read-only access to everything inside ops only, using the built-in Cluster Role view. Then create a token for the Service Account that is valid for one hour and save it to about slash answers slash token dot txt. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 2.6: sa token, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control create ns ops. Then kube control dash n ops create serviceaccount reporter. Then kube control dash n ops create rolebinding reporter view the clusterrole flag set to view the serviceaccount flag set to ops reporter. Then kube control dash n ops create token reporter the duration flag set to one hour about slash answers slash token dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Does R back have deny rules? Answer: No. It is purely additive; no matching allow means forbidden. Question two. What is the effect of a Cluster Role bound with a Role Binding? Answer: The permissions apply only inside the Role Binding's namespace. Question three. Which A P I group do you put for Deployments in a Role rule? Answer: apps (written deployments dot apps in the the resource flag flag).

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which command shows everything a user may do in a namespace? Answer: kube control auth can i the list flag dash n ns the as flag user. Question five. A Role Binding points to a Role with a misspelled name. Can you fix it with kube control edit? Answer: No; role Ref is immutable. Delete and recreate the binding. Question six. How do you get a one-hour token for a Service Account? Answer: kube control create token sa the duration flag set to one hour dash n ns.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. What do the C N and O fields of a client certificate mean to Kubernetes? Answer: C N is the user name, O is the group. Question eight. After the C S R is approved, where is the certificate? Answer: In dot status dot certificate of the Certificate Signing Request, base sixty-four encoded.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Objects: Role or Role Binding (namespace), Cluster Role or Cluster Role Binding (cluster). Scope trick: Cluster Role plus Role Binding equals one namespace only. Create: create role slash clusterrole the verb flag the resource flag; create rolebinding slash clusterrolebinding the user flag slash the group flag slash the serviceaccount flag ns name. Verify: auth can i verb resource dash n ns the as flag user. Immutable: role Ref of a binding: delete and recreate. Tokens: create token sa the duration flag set to one hour. Kubeconfig: set-cluster, set-credentials, set-context, use-context with the kube config flag. User cert: C S R signer Kubernetes dot io slash kube A P I server client, usage client auth, certificate approve. In the next module, we continue the course.
